Summarise columns

Source: R/summ.R
summ.Rd

Compute one row of summary statistics per selected variable and group. tabstat() delegates to summ() with .stat = "mean" by default; with .detail = TRUE and no explicit .stat, it returns all detail statistics.

Usage

summ(
  .data,
  ...,
  .by = NULL,
  .keep_all = FALSE,
  .detail = FALSE,
  .stat = character(0),
  .missing = TRUE,
  .name = FALSE,
  .type = c("list", "table"),
  .duration_format = c("long", "compact"),
  .sort = TRUE,
  .drop_empty = FALSE,
  .wt = NULL,
  .wt_type = c("frequency", "analytic")
)

tabstat(
  .data,
  ...,
  .by = NULL,
  .keep_all = FALSE,
  .detail = FALSE,
  .stat = "mean",
  .missing = TRUE,
  .name = FALSE,
  .type = c("list", "table"),
  .duration_format = c("long", "compact"),
  .sort = TRUE,
  .drop_empty = FALSE,
  .wt = NULL,
  .wt_type = c("frequency", "analytic")
)

Arguments

.data

A data frame, data frame extension (e.g. a tibble), or a vector. Matrix and data-frame columns are unsupported; use atomic or list columns. For sf input, summarise attribute data only: all geometry columns are removed before selection. Geometry columns cannot be selected or grouped.

...

Variables to summarise, using tidyselect or data-masking expressions (for example, dplyr::where(is.numeric) or x_sq = x^2). If omitted, select all columns except grouping keys.

.by

Optional grouping columns, selected with tidyselect. An explicit selection overrides existing group_by() groups; when omitted, existing groups are used. Grouping columns are excluded from the measured variables.

.keep_all

A single TRUE or FALSE. If FALSE (default), unsupported nonnumeric columns are removed with a warning; an error is raised if none of the selected columns can be summarised. If TRUE, character/list columns retain counts and unique values, with numeric statistics set to NA. Numeric-looking character values are not parsed.

.detail

A single TRUE or FALSE. If TRUE, return all statistics available for each variable type unless .stat selects a subset.

.stat

A character vector. If nonempty, return only the listed statistics, plus variable names, types and any grouping columns. Supported names are type, n, unique, miss_n, valid_pct, min, q1, median, mean, mad, sd, q3, max, iqr, skew, kurtosis, se, and sum. Aliases missing, p25, p50, and p75 select miss_n, q1, median, and q3; requested names and order are retained. Identical requested names are deduplicated; aliases and canonical names may coexist. sum applies to numeric summaries, not calendar dates or datetimes. Calendar summaries do not support skew or kurtosis either; when such a statistic is requested alongside numeric variables, calendar variables are skipped with a warning. Percentiles p0 through p100, including decimals such as p2.5, follow Stata's rule (see Details). Only requested statistics and their prerequisites are calculated when .stat is nonempty.

.missing

A single TRUE or FALSE. If TRUE (default), rows with a missing grouping key form their own group, like Stata's tabstat, by() missing. If FALSE, drop them before summarising. Missing measured values are always omitted from numeric statistics, regardless of this flag.

.name

A single TRUE or FALSE. If FALSE (default), drop the name column when exactly one measured variable is summarised, including zero-row grouped output; with several variables it is always kept. If TRUE, always retain it.

.type

The output container: "list" (default) or "table". "list" returns a single table when one variable-type family is present, otherwise a list named numeric, date, datetime, and/or time (for hms times of day). The numeric family also contains nonnumeric columns retained by .keep_all. "table" combines all families in one table. Calendar location columns are text, so a shared location column (such as mean) becomes character, with numeric values rounded to seven significant digits; counts remain numeric. Calendar spreads become plain numbers in days (Dates) or seconds (datetimes and times), and the unit is appended to type, for example "date [days]".

.duration_format

Retained for compatibility and no longer affects the output: calendar spreads are always difftime columns (see Details).

.sort

A single TRUE or FALSE. If TRUE (default), sort grouping keys ascending like tab() (factor levels in their defined order, character keys in C-locale order), with missing keys last. Within each group, preserve the selected variable order. If FALSE, groups follow first appearance.

.drop_empty

A single TRUE or FALSE. If TRUE, remove individual summary rows with no observed measured values (n == 0), even when n is not requested. This is independent of .missing. Default is FALSE.

.wt

Optional weights: a numeric column of .data (or a vector with one value per row), like Stata's summarize [fweight/aweight]. Rows with a missing weight are excluded with a message; negative weights are an error. When ... is omitted, the weight column is not summarised itself.

.wt_type

"frequency" (default) or "analytic". With frequency weights, n is the sum of the weights (non-integer weights are allowed). Analytic weights (Stata's [aweight], suitable for sampling weights) are rescaled within each group and variable to sum to the number of observed values, so n is the number of observations. Means, percentiles and sum are the same under both types; sd and se differ.

Value

A table, or a list of tables with .type = "list" when multiple variable-type families are present. Each table preserves the input's data.frame, tibble, or data.table container in both modes. Results are ungrouped, retaining grouping keys as columns and supported preview settings. Other subclasses are not reconstructed. Vector input returns a tibble in with .type = "list" or a data.frame with .type = "table", using its expression as the variable name, or value for a multiline expression or a magrittr pipe (.). Wrap the vector in a named tibble to choose a stable variable name. Input data are not modified.

Details

Counts and missing values:

n counts observed values and unique counts distinct observed values. miss_n counts missing values; valid_pct is the fraction observed, from zero to one, and is NA for zero-row inputs. Missingness follows the original vector's is.na() method, including SPSS user-missing values and ranges. Retained list columns count complete element identities without flattening. Columns with no observed values remain in the result: n and unique are zero and location/spread statistics, including sum, are NA. Zero-row grouped inputs do not create artificial groups.

Numeric statistics:

Numeric calculations use double precision. Large integer64 values may lose precision during conversion, with a warning.

Logical values are treated as zero/one. Factors and ordered factors use their underlying level codes with a warning. Numeric labelled vectors use underlying values, excluding user-missing codes; label metadata is flagged with a warning. Measured vectors and difftime use their original units. In variable names, * marks labelled vectors, ** marks factors and *** marks retained nonnumeric columns.

Statistics follow Stata's summarize, detail and are tested against Stata's own output:

  • SD uses the sample denominator (n - 1); se is SD divided by sqrt(n).

  • Percentiles use Stata's rule, not R's default stats::quantile() type 7: with n sorted values, the pth percentile is the value at position floor(n * p) + 1, or the mean of the values at positions n * p and n * p + 1 when n * p is whole. So q1 of 1:4 is 1.5 (type 7 gives 1.75). median, q1, q3 and iqr (q3 - q1) use the same rule.

  • skew and kurtosis use population moments, m3 / m2^1.5 and m4 / m2^2, so kurtosis is 3 for a normal distribution (not excess kurtosis). They are NA when the values are constant or fewer than two.

  • mad has no Stata counterpart; it uses stats::mad() with its default scaling.

For singleton or constant inputs, undefined spread statistics are NA.

Weighted statistics:

With .wt, the mean is sum(w * x) / W and the variance is sum(w * (x - mean)^2) / (W - 1), where W is the summed weight (after rescaling for analytic weights); se is sd / sqrt(W), and sum is sum(w * x) with the weights as given, as Stata's r(sum), even for analytic weights. Percentiles, median, q1, q3, iqr and mad use Stata's weighted percentile rule, the unweighted rule with cumulative weights in place of positions, so weights of 1 give the unweighted values. min and max ignore rows with zero weight. unique, miss_n and valid_pct remain unweighted row counts.

Calendar output and grouping names:

Date locations are displayed as YYYY-MM-DD; fractional days are not shown. Infinite Date locations are displayed as -Inf or Inf; missing locations remain NA. Datetime locations are displayed as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM, without seconds, in the variable's own time zone (the session time zone when none is set). hms time-of-day locations are displayed as hh:mm:ss.

Calendar spread statistics (sd, se, mad, iqr) are difftime columns, so they can be compared across rows and used in arithmetic. Each column has one unit: days for Dates; for datetimes and times, the unit (seconds, minutes, hours or days) that fits the column's median nonzero spread. Convert with, for example, as.numeric(out$sd, units = "hours"). Grouping keys that collide with summary metadata or internal pivot names are renamed by prepending dots until unique among the input names, with a message. The input data are not modified.

Examples

summ(lifeexp)
#> Warning: country is non-numeric and thus removed.
#> Warning: region is a labelled variable (*).
#> # A tibble: 5 × 8
#>   name      type        n unique   min     mean        sd     max
#>   <chr>     <chr>   <int>  <int> <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1 *region   dbl+lbl    68      3   1      1.5       0.743     3  
#> 2 popgrowth dbl        68     32  -2.5    0.553     1.06      2.6
#> 3 lexp      dbl        68     20  57     71.7       5.16     79  
#> 4 gnppc     dbl        67     64 170   9137.    11497.    46650  
#> 5 safewater dbl        54     32  36     77.2      20.6     100  
summ(lifeexp, .by = region)
#> Warning: country is non-numeric and thus removed.
#> # A tibble: 12 × 9
#>    region               name     type      n unique   min    mean      sd    max
#>    <dbl+lbl>            <chr>    <chr> <int>  <int> <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>  <dbl>

#>  3 1 [Europe & C. Asia] gnppc    dbl      43     42 170   1.13e+4 1.29e+4 4.66e4
#>  4 1 [Europe & C. Asia] safewat… dbl      42     25  36   8.16e+1 1.86e+1 1   e2
#>  5 2 [North America]    popgrow… dbl      14     11   0.3 1.33e+0 7.80e-1 2.6 e0
#>  6 2 [North America]    lexp     dbl      14     13  57   6.97e+1 6.14e+0 7.9 e1
#>  7 2 [North America]    gnppc    dbl      14     14 410   6.29e+3 9.08e+3 3.20e4
#>  8 2 [North America]    safewat… dbl       6      5  40   5.8 e+1 2.40e+1 9.9 e1
#>  9 3 [South America]    popgrow… dbl      10      7   0.5 1.59e+0 4.89e-1 2.2 e0

#> 12 3 [South America]    safewat… dbl       6      6  45   6.53e+1 1.70e+1 9.1 e1
tabstat(lifeexp, .by = region)
#> Warning: country is non-numeric and thus removed.
#> # A tibble: 12 × 4
#>    region               name      type        mean
#>    <dbl+lbl>            <chr>     <chr>      <dbl>
#>  1 1 [Europe & C. Asia] popgrowth dbl       0.0705
#>  2 1 [Europe & C. Asia] lexp      dbl      72.5   
#>  3 1 [Europe & C. Asia] gnppc     dbl   11284.    
#>  4 1 [Europe & C. Asia] safewater dbl      81.6   
#>  5 2 [North America]    popgrowth dbl       1.33  
#>  6 2 [North America]    lexp      dbl      69.7   
#>  7 2 [North America]    gnppc     dbl    6294.    
#>  8 2 [North America]    safewater dbl      58     
#>  9 3 [South America]    popgrowth dbl       1.59  
#> 10 3 [South America]    lexp      dbl      70.7   
#> 11 3 [South America]    gnppc     dbl    3881     
#> 12 3 [South America]    safewater dbl      65.3   

# Weighted summaries, like Stata's summarize [aweight = w]
survey <- tibble::tibble(income = c(10, 20, 40), w = c(3, 1, 1))
summ(survey, income, .wt = w, .stat = c("n", "mean", "sd", "p50"))
#> # A tibble: 1 × 5
#>   type      n  mean    sd   p50
#>   <chr> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 dbl       5    18  13.0    10
summ(survey, income, .wt = w, .wt_type = "analytic", .stat = c("n", "sd"))
#> # A tibble: 1 × 3
#>   type      n    sd
#>   <chr> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 dbl       3  14.3

lifeexp |>
  summ(
    dplyr::where(is.numeric),
    .by = region,
    .stat = c("n", "mean", "sd", "p50")
  )

# Keep numeric and calendar summaries in separate tables
mixed <- tibble::tibble(x = c(1, 3), day = as.Date("2024-01-01") + 0:1)
summ(mixed, .type = "list")
#> A list is returned as statistics are heterogeneous.
#> $numeric
#> # A tibble: 1 × 8
#>   name  type      n unique   min  mean    sd   max
#>   <chr> <chr> <int>  <int> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 x     dbl       2      2     1     2  1.41     3
#> 
#> $date
#> # A tibble: 1 × 8
#>   name  type      n unique mean       sd             min        max       
#>   <chr> <chr> <int>  <int> <chr>      <drtn>         <chr>      <chr>     
#> 1 day   date      2      2 2024-01-01 0.7071068 days 2024-01-01 2024-01-02
#> 

# Choose a stable variable name when starting from a vector
scores <- c(4, 6, NA, 8)
tibble::tibble(score = scores) |> summ(.name = TRUE)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 8
#>   name  type      n unique   min  mean    sd   max
#>   <chr> <chr> <int>  <int> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 score dbl       3      3     4     6     2     8
